summary: DecoratedCookie is a specialized kind of Cookie. It inherits everything a Cookie has and knows, then replaces the describe method with a message about sprinkles and icing.

lines.text: The `extends` keyword makes DecoratedCookie a subclass of Cookie, so it automatically has the flavor field and every method Cookie defines.
A subclass does not inherit constructors, so DecoratedCookie needs its own that accepts the flavor the caller wants.
This hands the flavor up to the Cookie constructor, which is where the field is actually stored. A call to `super(...)` must be the first statement in the constructor.
This annotation tells the compiler you intend to replace a method from the parent class. If the name or parameters do not match, compilation fails instead of quietly adding a new method.
Because this method has the same signature as Cookie's describe, calling describe() on a DecoratedCookie runs this version instead of the inherited one.

lines.code: return "This " + getFlavor() + " cookie is decorated with sprinkles and icing!";
lines.text: The flavor is read through the inherited getter rather than the field directly, which is how a subclass reaches private data in its parent.
